criteria.commensurate: For D4, yes: about +10% of the 17.7 s total buys a mean house-to-field distance of 355-394 ft against 416-443 on main (research R1), the GM's stated behavior. For the residual 0.9 s (+5%), no: an identical-answer change recovers it (below), so it buys nothing.
criteria.necessary: Mostly. D4 (seat nearest the field, 16 directions x 3 rings at once) is the GM's canon ruling of 2026-10-03 and costs 2.06 s of homestead CPU at 15 hh (7.66 -> 5.60 with it reverted; bookend 20.5 -> 18.6). The windows (correction 1) now cost nothing over main-sized boxes (7.66 vs 7.67, same houses). The 40-hh web growth is the layout (seed 4 web 2.88 landed, 2.71 with 318's web code stubbed, 1.55 main). The search with no radius is FR-003, but the ~1 s it costs is not: it comes from how the first house's candidates are tested, not from the rule.
criteria.no_way_around: There is a cheaper way for the residual. capacity.free_seats lists every grid point on the canvas for the first house and calls fg.point_taken on each one. About 26k points per seed fall past the seating window, and each is decided by FreeGround._cell_beyond with one scalar shapely.box plus contains/disjoint (110,873 new cells, 1.3 s timed, called from free_seats -> grow_the_margin). The fix: before the loop, decide those cells in ONE vectorized shapely.contains(region, boxes)/shapely.disjoint(grown, boxes) call over the same cells and fill fg._beyond. Measured on 8a374693f (3 runs each): 7.81/7.87/7.63 -> 6.84/6.83/6.82 s, with house hashes identical on all four seeds (8212a77c 1710d203 937a8877 d6db8c21), so the answers are the same by construction. Making the candidates lazy, nearest first, would be cheaper still. D4 has no cheaper equivalent among those measured (R1). Even with the fix the total stays band 3 (about +10%, all of it D4), which needs the GM's perf-signoff.
